```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 1](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop1.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the `command_line` folder:

```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
pwd
```

Replace the text below each heading with your own notes. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk like the one above.

## Basic unix commands

Notes on `pwd`, `ls`, `cd` and how unix commands are put together.
cd - change directory
pwd - print working directory

```{bash}
ls -l
```

```{bash}
ls -lr
```

```{bash}
ls -l /usr
```

creating the fasta file
```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
echo $'>fasta_header\nMMGTSRCVILLFALLLWAANAAPPEIHTTRPNVPEEIKRPNSTEIETPAVKQLETPSIFL\nLTTLEVAEADVDSTLETMKDRNKKNSAKLSKIGNNMKSLLSVFSVFGGFLSLLSVVTTTS' > test.fasta
```


## Viewing and searching files

Notes on `cat`, `head`, `grep` and `man`.

cat is used to view the file 

```{bash}
cat test.fasta
```

head is used to look at few lines of the file if file is huge. 
head usually displays the first 10 lines and -2 only displays the first 2 lines 

```{bash}
head -2 test.fasta
```

grep - globally search a regular expression and print
grep - finds line matching specific strings in files

- to find the fasta header - include quotes in the command
```{bash}
grep '^>' test.fasta
```

- finding a specific amino acid sequence
```{bash}
grep KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta
```
man grep - view the flags
```{bash}
man grep
```

grep has approx. 50 flags
some of the flags:
1. -i -> case insensitive match
2. -n -> report line number of matches
3. -c -> count all files that contain the pattern
4. -w -> match whole words only

using the -n command it will give the line on which the flag is
```{bash}
grep -n KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta
```

## Sequence file formats

Notes on the fasta and fastq formats.
FASTA - creates and stores a clean, finished reference sequences - like final textbook 
FASTQ - stores raw data straight from sequencer incl. error-check quality scores (like rough field notes).

example of FASTA (clean and simple)
- >Reference_Sequence_01
 ATCGATCGATCGATCGATCG
 
• 2 lines per record
	1. Header line starting with >
	2. Sequence data (DNA, RNA, or amino acids)
	
example of FASTQ (Raw & Includes Quality Scores)
- @ Sequencer_Read_01
ATCGATCGATCGATCGATCG
+
FFFFFGGGGGIIIIIRRRRR

• 4 lines per record
1. Header line starting with @
2. Sequence data (nucleotides)
3. Separator line starting with +
